description: After David ran /exit, Master completed the exit sequence but held the final commit step, asking David to say 'commit' before it would run, citing the no-auto-commit-on-exit feedback. David pushed back: 'Why is everything not committed?' An explicit exit signal from David is a request to run the full exit protocol including the commit; the standing feedback rejected unattended automatic commit machinery (hooks), not committing when David himself initiates the exit.
correction: Spawn Rigby immediately to stage and commit the working tree via the git skill. Updated the feedback memory to clarify: explicit exit (conversational or /exit) routes to the commit path; when in doubt mid-exit, commit rather than hold.
systemic_fix: The no-auto-commit rule governs unattended automation, not David-initiated exits. On any explicit exit signal, run the complete exit protocol including the commit, and report what was committed. Only hold a commit when automation would be the actor without David's initiation.
